subject: CFA with categorical data and structured missingness

messages.author: 8f3e92578c92b5ea
messages.subject: CFA with categorical data and structured missingness
parts:
Hello,
  I'm working on a set of confirmatory factor analyses of a set of items that have structured missingness. I know that this not ideal and it is relatively common among clinical measures.

The items are scored 0, 1, 2 as ordered categories. If you respond as a 2 on any of items 1-3, then items 4-10 administered. If you respond as a 0 or 1 on all of items 1-3, then items 4-10 are not administered. Approximately 30% of items 4-10 are missing. Conceptually the idea is that if you fail to pass the first 3 screening items, then you will not endorse any of the later items. In practice, I often see people just recoding these missing items as 0s. Recently, I've come across literature suggesting this is bad because it inflates the correlations among the items which could artificially reduce dimensionality in the factor structure.

I've fit the model a few different ways:
1) Code additional items as 0 with wlsmvs
cfa(model = mod.a, data = data, estimator = "WLSMVS", std.lv = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, ordered = c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "a5", "a6", "a7", "a8", "a9", "a10")
2) Leave additional items as missing and run wlsmvs with missing = "pairwise
cfa(model = mod.a, data = data, estimator = "WLSMVS", std.lv = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, ordered = c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "a5", "a6", "a7", "a8", "a9", "a10")
3) Treat it more like an IRT model (estimator = "MML")
cfa(model = mod.a, data = data, estimator = "MML", std.lv = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, ordered = c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "a5", "a6", "a7", "a8", "a9", "a10")

I've also considered doing multiple imputation of items 4-10 and then running WLSMVS on the imputed dataframes.

From a results perspective,
1) Additional items as 0 with wlsmvs, gets cfi = .999, rmsea = .043, and very high factor loadings (lowest is > .7).
2) Additional items as missing with WLSMVS & missing = "pairwise", cfi = .977, rmsea = .06, and moderate factor loadings (.52 - .84).
3) estimator = "MML", no CFI/RMSEA provided, loadings rnge from .59 - 1.462 (I think these are actually discrimination parameters and not directly equivalent to a factor loading).

I haven't been able to find a clear answer on which approach is best. If anyone can provide feedback on which might be the best option (or if there is a best option that I haven't considered), help would be much appreciated.

Thank you,
Andrew

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: CFA with categorical data and structured missingness
parts: If you respond as a 0 or 1 on all of items 1-3, then items 4-10 are not administered.
So that means they are missing by design, conditional on the observed data (items 1-3).  That is a MAR situation.

2) Leave additional items as missing and run wlsmvs with missing = "pairwise
cfa(model = mod.a, data = data, estimator = "WLSMVS", std.lv = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, ordered = c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "a5", "a6", "a7", "a8", "a9", "a10")
This uses all available information to estimate each polychoric correlation, which I think is valid in your case.

3) Treat it more like an IRT model (estimator = "MML")
cfa(model = mod.a, data = data, estimator = "MML", std.lv = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, ordered = c("a1", "a2", "a3", "a4", "a5", "a6", "a7", "a8", "a9", "a10")
If this works in tandem with missing = 'FIML', then that would return unbiased results.
I've also considered doing multiple imputation of items 4-10 and then running WLSMVS on the imputed dataframes.

That would work too.  MI with infinite imputations produces equivalent results as FIML when the imputation model has the same information as the FIML analysis.
